sheets.failure_mode: The dangerous half fails open: an issue body is untrusted text written by anyone on the internet, and with no one to prompt, instructions embedded in it reach a model that already has repo write scope. The safe half fails closed and silently: anything not pre-approved is refused, and a triage run that quietly does nothing looks the same as a healthy one unless the job asserts on its own output. Duplicate detection is also inherently model-judgement, so false positives land as public comments.
sheets.version_caveat: The documentation mirror available here has no GitHub Actions page, so the action's own version, plan, and permission requirements are unverified and I will not guess them. One gate is confirmable and directly relevant: the ultracode workflow keyword no longer triggers from a relayed webhook payload or pull request comment as of Claude Code v2.1.210, so on older versions an issue body containing that keyword could start a large workflow run inside the triage job.

sheets.primary: A GitHub Action workflow triggered on issues opened, running Claude Code headless in the runner with a triage prompt and a narrow tool allowlist, using the gh CLI or the GitHub API to apply labels, search for duplicates and post the first-response comment. The no-human-at-a-terminal requirement is what rules out every session-scoped mechanism.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A local hook or a scheduled agent on a developer machine, rejected because both still depend on somebody's machine being up and a session existing, which is not an unattended CI path.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness side, in the form of CI: the workflow trigger, the job permissions and the token scope are what actually bound the run. The model owns only the triage judgement inside those bounds.
sheets.context_boundary: A fresh, ephemeral context per workflow run, living entirely inside the runner. The issue title and body plus whatever repo context the prompt pulls in cross inward; labels, a duplicate list and a comment cross outward through the API. Nothing persists between runs.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts on the issues opened event and ends when the job exits. There is no state carried forward, so duplicate detection must query the repository each time rather than relying on memory.
sheets.failure_mode: The issue body is attacker-controlled text going straight into an automated agent, so prompt injection is the headline risk and the mitigation is least-privilege token scope plus a tool allowlist, not model instructions. Otherwise it fails open harmlessly: a failed run leaves the issue untriaged and someone notices, whereas an over-permissioned run can mislabel, close or comment wrongly at scale with nobody watching.
sheets.version_caveat: This needs an API key or OAuth token stored as a repository secret and the action pinned to a specific version rather than a floating tag; I do not know the current action version or its exact input names from model knowledge, so those must be read off the action's own repository before the workflow is written.

sheets.primary: A GitHub Action in the repository's workflow config, triggered on the issues opened event, running Claude Code non-interactively in the CI runner with a prompt that labels the issue, searches open issues for likely duplicates, and posts the first-response comment through the GitHub API with a scoped token. GitHub Actions is the documented option for tasks tied to repo events that should live alongside the workflow config, and it is the only one of the options that needs no machine of yours to be awake.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A Routine (an Anthropic-managed scheduled or event-triggered run configured at claude.ai/code/routines). It can also fire on GitHub events without a terminal, but the triage logic should be versioned and reviewed in the same repository as the workflow it serves, and it needs the runner's checkout and repo credentials.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness, in the sense that the CI system owns the trigger and the run: the webhook fires the job whether or not any model judges the issue interesting. The content of the triage (which label, which duplicate, what the comment says) is model-owned and unreviewed, which is the part with no guarantee attached.
sheets.context_boundary: An ephemeral context per issue, inside the runner. The issue title and body and whatever duplicate search results the job gathers cross in; labels and a comment cross out to GitHub. Nothing carries over to the next issue or into any developer's local session, so give the job everything it needs in the prompt.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts on the issues opened webhook and ends when the job exits; there is no session to resume and no state between runs. It stops applying when the workflow file is removed or disabled, or when the event filter no longer matches.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open: if the job errors, the API rate-limits, or the token lacks the scope, the issue is simply left untriaged and nobody at a terminal notices. The more expensive failure is silent wrongness, since a mislabel or a confidently wrong duplicate claim is posted publicly with no human in the loop; keep the token least-privilege, make the first-response comment hedged, and prefer suggesting a duplicate over closing one.
sheets.version_caveat: I cannot state the action's version, plan, or authentication requirements from my permitted inputs: the documentation mirror I have does not include the GitHub Actions page, only a pointer to it from the scheduling comparison. One caveat I can state from the mirror: as of v2.1.210 the ultracode keyword does not start a dynamic workflow when it arrives via a webhook payload or a pull request comment relayed into the conversation, or via a -p prompt, so untrusted issue text cannot escalate the run that way; before v2.1.210 it could.

sheets.primary: A GitHub Action running Claude Code in the repository's CI, wired to the issue-opened workflow trigger, with a prompt that labels the issue, searches for likely duplicates and posts the first response. The documentation routes repo-event automation to Actions rather than to any in-session mechanism.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A hook. Every hook event is anchored to a point in a Claude Code session lifecycle, and there is no session at the moment a GitHub issue is opened, so no hook can serve as the trigger.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness owns invocation, since the CI runner starts the job on the repo event, but the model owns the outcome: the label choice, the duplicate judgement and the comment text are all judgement calls made with nobody available to ask.
sheets.context_boundary: A fresh context window per run inside the CI job, with no continuity between issues. What crosses in is the issue payload plus whatever the run reads from the repository or the GitHub API; what crosses out is the label change and the posted comment.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts on the configured repository event, runs to completion, and its context is discarded when the job ends. It stops applying when the workflow file is removed or its trigger no longer matches the event.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory in substance and fails open operationally. The run is autonomous and cannot ask a clarifying question, so an ambiguous issue yields a confidently wrong label or a wrong duplicate claim, published without review. A failed job usually means no triage rather than a blocked issue, so the miss is invisible unless someone watches workflow status.
sheets.version_caveat: Unconfirmed from my permitted inputs: the documentation mirror contains no GitHub Actions page, so I will not assert an action version, input name or plan restriction. The one gate I can confirm is credentials, since a CI run needs a long-lived token from `claude setup-token`, which requires a Claude subscription, or an API key instead.

scenarios.scenario: Before the agent ends its turn and declares work complete, the test suite must have actually been run and passed during that turn; if not, the agent should be sent back to keep working. This must hold even when the model simply forgets to test.

key.primary: Stop hook that verifies tests ran and passed, and on failure exits 2 (or returns decision "block" with a reason) so Claude must continue working
key.rejected_alternative: A PostToolUse hook on Edit that reminds Claude to run the tests
key.rejection_reason: PostToolUse fires per tool call and cannot gate the end of the turn; it never fires at all when the model declares completion without making another tool call. Stop is the documented event for enforcing validation before accepting a response: its block decision prevents Claude from stopping and feeds the reason back so the conversation continues.
key.lifecycle: Stop event fires when Claude finishes responding; exit code 2 or decision "block" prevents the turn from ending and injects the reason
key.failure_mode: A hook that blocks unconditionally traps the agent in an infinite continue loop; the script needs a termination condition (such as checking the repeat-invocation flag in the hook input) or the session never ends.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook that verifies an artifact the harness produced during this turn, for example a marker file written by a PostToolUse Bash hook when the test command exits zero, or by running the suite itself, and returns {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."} to push Claude back into work when the evidence is absent.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A skill or CLAUDE.md instruction saying to always run tests before declaring done. That is the stated failure: the requirement explicitly has to hold when the model simply forgets, and guidance has no checkpoint at the end of the turn.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split, with the harness owning the gate: Claude Code decides whether the turn may end based on the hook's exit, while the model owns actually getting the suite green once it is sent back.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs in its own process outside the conversation and receives stop_hook_active, last_assistant_message, transcript_path, background_tasks, and session_crons on stdin. Only the reason string, or an additionalContext string, crosses back into the model's context, capped at 10,000 characters.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires when the main agent has finished responding, once per turn. It does not fire when the user interrupts, and a turn ended by an API error fires StopFailure instead. It stops applying after eight consecutive blocks, when Claude Code overrides the hook and lets the turn end.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open in two ways. Any non-zero exit other than 2 is a non-blocking error, so a crashed or misconfigured hook lets the turn end silently; and the eight-block cap eventually releases a turn that never satisfies the condition. A hook that infers success by grepping the transcript for a test command also fails open on a model that only claimed to run it, which is why the check must read a harness-produced artifact. The opposite risk is a block loop, which is what stop_hook_active exists to break.
sheets.version_caveat: No plan restriction or experimental gate on Stop decision control. The background_tasks and session_crons input arrays, useful for distinguishing "done" from "paused waiting on a background test run", require Claude Code v2.1.145 or later. /goal is the built-in session-scoped equivalent if you would rather not ship hook configuration.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook. The deterministic shape is a pair: a PostToolUse hook on Bash writes a pass marker (session id, turn boundary, timestamp, exit status) when the test command succeeds, and a command-type Stop hook checks for a marker belonging to the turn that is ending and returns {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."} when it is absent, which sends the reason back as Claude's next instruction. Where the check must inspect real state rather than a marker, use an agent-type Stop hook that runs the suite itself.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A CLAUDE.md or rules instruction saying to always run tests before declaring work complete. That is the exact instruction the model forgets, so restating it more emphatically does not change the enforcement class.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split by design: the harness fires Stop and enforces the block, but the model owns the remediation because only it can go run the tests and fix what fails. The hook can refuse the ending, not produce a passing suite.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs out-of-process and receives stop_hook_active, last_assistant_message, background_tasks and transcript_path on stdin. Only the reason or additionalContext string crosses back into the same session's context window, where it becomes the model's next instruction. An agent-type hook runs its verification in a separate subagent context and returns only ok plus reason.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires every time the main agent finishes responding, which is not the same as task completion, so it fires on conversational turns too. It does not fire on a user interrupt, and API errors route to StopFailure instead. The marker must be scoped to the current turn or the hook goes stale and passes a turn that ran tests an hour earlier.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed at first and then degrades to fail open: Claude Code overrides the hook and ends the turn after 8 consecutive blocks, so a hook that never converges eventually lets the unverified turn through. A hook that ignores stop_hook_active will hit that cap on every run. A marker-file design is also gameable in the weak sense that the model can satisfy it by running a trivially narrow subset of tests.
sheets.version_caveat: No version gate on command-type Stop hooks. Agent-type hooks are explicitly experimental and may change, with a 60 second default timeout and a 50 tool-turn ceiling; prompt-type hooks default to 30 seconds and judge only from the hook input. CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP raises the 8-block cap, and /goal is the built-in session-scoped shortcut for a prompt-based Stop hook if you want the behavior without config.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook whose handler proves from the turn's transcript, or from a marker file the test runner writes, that the suite ran and passed during this turn, and returns decision "block" with a reason (or hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext) when it cannot.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A skill or CLAUDE.md rule instructing the agent to run tests before declaring completion. Rejected because the stated failure is precisely the model forgetting, and advisory guidance has no hold on a turn that is already ending.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split, with the harness owning the gate. Claude Code fires Stop and honours the block, so the turn cannot end, but the model still owns actually running the suite once it is sent back.
sheets.context_boundary: The handler runs outside the model context, reading transcript_path and last_assistant_message from stdin. Only the reason or additionalContext string crosses back, rendered as hook feedback in the transcript.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires every time the main agent finishes responding, including on turns that had nothing to do with code. It does not fire on a user interrupt, and a turn ended by an API error goes to StopFailure instead.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open under repetition: Claude Code overrides the hook and ends the turn after 8 consecutive blocks, and any exit code other than 2 is a non-blocking error. It can also loop if the handler ignores stop_hook_active, and it only ever verifies evidence that tests ran, not that the change is correct.
sheets.version_caveat: No version gate on the Stop event. Telling 'session finished' apart from 'paused waiting on a background test run' needs the background_tasks and session_crons input fields, available from v2.1.145, and the eight block cap is raised with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP.

sheets.primary: A Stop hook that checks for hard evidence that the suite ran and passed inside this turn (a results file or marker whose mtime is newer than the turn start, or a fresh exit-status record written by a PostToolUse hook on the test command) and, when the evidence is absent, blocks the stop and returns a reason telling the agent to run the tests.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A verification-before-completion skill or a CLAUDE.md rule; both are advisory, and the scenario explicitly requires holding when the model forgets, which is the exact case instructions do not cover.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness owns the gate: it refuses to let the turn end. The model still owns the remediation work once it is sent back.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs in its own process and sees only the session metadata and transcript path, not the model's reasoning; the blocking reason string is what crosses back and it is injected as new input, so the model continues in the same context window with the reason appended.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires each time the agent tries to end its turn, for every session where the hook is configured; it must short-circuit when the stop-hook-active flag is already set, otherwise it re-triggers itself, and it stops applying when the evidence check passes or the hook is removed.
sheets.failure_mode: Two real failures: an infinite block loop if the guard flag is not honoured or the evidence can never be produced, and a false pass if the check is weak (a stale results file, or trusting a transcript grep for the string 'tests passed' which the model can emit without running anything). If the hook itself errors and exits zero it fails open and the turn ends unverified.
sheets.version_caveat: The Stop hook's structured output (the block decision and the flag that says a stop hook already ran) is a JSON-shaped contract that has evolved; exit-code-only blocking behaves differently from the JSON form. I cannot pin the version where the JSON decision fields landed, so the hook should be validated against the installed build.
